correctness.rationale: Fejér–Riesz turns the continuous problem into the path-adjacency Rayleigh quotient, giving 2cos(π/(n+2)) and the sine-eigenvector extremizer. Its polynomial identity identifies the complete contact set. The displayed positive contact weights satisfy the constant, first and higher cosine moment equations, proving equality when all contacts lie on the grid. Conversely finite-LP equality forces any dual measure onto those zeros; after symmetrizing, Chebyshev moments through degree n uniquely determine the positive aggregate weights on the distinct contact cosines. Hence every contact cosine is sampled. The contacts at fractions 3/(2R) and 5/(2R), R=n+2, force the lcm denominator 2R to divide N. Fresh independent replay verified all contact moment identities for n=3,…,30 and the contact-inclusion equivalence for 4,116 grid pairs.

value.rationale: The finite cyclic problem is a canonical relaxation of the classical Carathéodory–Fejér extremum. An exact all-degree classification of zero-loss meshes, together with the contact-set rigidity mechanism, is reusable structural information for discrete positive-definite and sampling problems rather than a numerical case list.

final_claim: For the full degree-n Carathéodory–Fejér interval problem with n≥3, cyclic sampling on N points preserves the continuous optimum 2cos(π/(n+2)) exactly when 2(n+2) divides N; every other mesh has a strictly larger sampled optimum, possibly infinite under aliasing.
limitations: The theorem treats the full harmonic interval and n≥3; degree two and singleton-harmonic problems are separate.
It classifies equality with the continuous optimum, not a closed formula for every strict off-mesh excess.
An older equivalent result could be phrased in circulant positive-definite, Toeplitz linear-programming, or graph-theoretic theta language.
